chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid from Abu Jamilah from Zayd al-Shahham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who was fasting and thought that night had entered and that the sun had set, and there was clouds in the sky, so he broke his fast, then the clouds cleared and behold the sun had not set, he said: 'His fast is complete and he does not have to make it up.'

key_terms.وَلَا يَقْضِيهِ: And he does not make it up

ai.seo_question: Does a person need to make up their fast if they broke it thinking the sun had set due to clouds?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of 'al-ghalat' (reasonable error) in fasting, where the presence of clouds obscuring the sun constitutes a valid excuse for breaking the fast. It demonstrates the Shia juristic emphasis on subjective certainty (yaqin) over objective reality when the cause of doubt is natural phenomena, thereby exempting the individual from both making up the fast (qada) and offering expiation (kaffarah).
